column1: # The fourteen Māheśvara sūtras — task B-046, doc 01 §2.
# AUTHORED. This is a 2500-year-old text and the one file in spec/ that cannot
# be derived from anything: no oracle emits it and no measurement produces it.
# It is transcribed here from the standard recension rather than vendored, so
# the project owns its own copy under its own licence.
# The last entry of each line is the ANUBANDHA (it-marker) — a boundary sign,
# not a sound. Everything else is a phoneme. A pratyāhāra is then simply a
# range: start at some phoneme, run forward, stop at a named marker, and drop
# the markers passed on the way. अच् is every phoneme from अ to the marker च्,
# which is the nine vowels; हल् is every phoneme from ह to the marker ल्, which
# That is the whole mechanism, and it is why the ordering is not arbitrary: the
# sūtras are arranged so that the classes a grammar needs are contiguous.
# ह appears TWICE, in sūtra 5 and sūtra 14, and that is not a transcription
# error — it is what lets हल् cover the consonants while अच् stops short of
# them. A pratyāhāra starting at ह takes the first occurrence.
